rows.speaker: القاشاني
rows.claim: Al-Qashani reads nūn as the universal soul and the Pen as the universal intellect; the first is alluded to by its initial letter, the second likened to a pen inscribing forms in a tablet.
rows.anchor: ن هو النفس الكلية والقلم هو العقل الكلي والأول من باب الكناية بالاكتفاء من الكلمة

rows.speaker: القاشاني
rows.claim: What is written comprises forms, configurations, and destined states of things; intermediate intellects and holy spirits are its scribes, though God is the true writer and their agency is metaphorically attributed in the realm of the Divine Names.
rows.anchor: وما يسطرون من صور الأشياء وما هيأتها وأحوالها المقدرة على ما تقع عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath by the Pen, the soul, and what they write suits the sworn statement because these are noble, encompass existence at the first level of influence, and are principles of existence and divine determination.
rows.anchor: لشرفهما وكونما مشتملين على كل الوجود في أول مرتبة التأثير والتأثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ in bi-niʿmati is attached to an omitted circumstantial expression describing the pronoun in the predicate majnūn; its governor is the sense of negation.
rows.anchor: والباء متعلقة بمضمر هو حال من الضمير في خبر ما وهو مجنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Madness is a barrier between soul and intellect; the word may describe being struck by jinn or the heart, or having soul and intellect separated.
rows.anchor: والجنون حائل بين النفس والعقل وجن فلان أي أصابه الجن أوأصاب جنانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is entirely free of the madness charged against him by hostile, envious deniers; by God's favor he is endowed with prophethood and general leadership.
rows.anchor: أنت بريء منه ملتبسا بنعمة الله التي هي النبوة والرياسة العامة

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān calls the phrase an oath interposed between subject and predicate to intensify the denial of the Prophet's vile alleged trait.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حيان قوله : بنعمة ربك قسم اعترض به بين المحكوم عليه والحكم

rows.speaker: نجم الدين
rows.claim: Najm al-Dīn also treats the phrase as an oath in his Taʾwīlāt.
rows.anchor: حضرة الشيخ نجم الدين في تأويلاته روى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report recounts the Prophet's first revelation at Ḥirāʾ, Gabriel teaching him prayer, Khadīja consulting Waraqa, and Quraysh later calling him mad; God swore he was not mad. The passage says the sūra's first five verses were among the earliest revealed.
rows.anchor: غاب عن خديجة رضي الله عنها إلى حراء فلم تجده فإذا هو قد طلع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the first revelation was the command to glorify the Lord, and this verse was the second.
rows.anchor: أول ما نزل قوله سبح اسم ربك وهذه الآية هي الثانية

rows.speaker: نجم الدين
rows.claim: In the Najmiyya reading, the Prophet is not veiled from what was eternally past or will be eternally future: jinn means concealment, while his knowledge encompasses both; the excerpt begins citing a gesture as evidence.
rows.anchor: ما أنت بنعمة ربك بمستور عما كان من الأزل وما سيكون إلى الأبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian admonitory verse says that words without deeds are false, a sleeper cannot awaken another sleeper, and counsel must be heard attentively.
rows.anchor: كفت عالم بكوش جان بشنو ور نماند بكفتنش كردار باطلست آنكه مدعى كويد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once the foregoing is clear, the Prophet must persist in refusing their demand that he stop confronting them; he is ordered to stand firm despite his small following and their large numbers.
rows.anchor: فدم على ما أنت عليه من عدم طاعتهم فيما يدعونك إليه من الكف عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows that obeying a disobedient person is itself disobedience, and yielding to a tyrant is transgression.
rows.anchor: دلت الآية على أن الإطاعة للعاصي عصيان والافتداء بالطاغي طغيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Law is optative here; idhān, originally akin to oiling and derived from oil, means leniency, accommodation, or abandoning a firm position.
rows.anchor: لو للتمني والإدهان في الأصل مثل التدهين واشتقاقهما من الدهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their hoped-for response is that they would then refrain from attacking or criticizing the Prophet.
rows.anchor: أي فهم يداهنونك حينئذ بترك الطعن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On one parsing, fa coordinates yad-hinūna with the optative clause, so it stays indicative rather than losing nūn as a subjunctive result.
rows.anchor: فالفاء للعطف على تدهن فيكون يدهنون داخلا في حيز لو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, fa marks consequence: they would accommodate him as a result of his accommodating them; the verb can also describe their present flattery in hope of his compromise.
rows.anchor: أو الفاء للسببية فهو مسبب ن تدهن ويجوز أن يكون الفعل للحال

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kāshifī paraphrases the verse as a refusal to obey polytheists who invite the Prophet to his forefathers' religion; they want him to soften his criticism of their idolatry so they will reciprocate and stop taunting his faith.
rows.anchor: كما قال الكاشفي) : فرمان مبر مشركان كه راكه ترا بدين آباء

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some advise that outward conduct should agree with inward conviction; outward compliance without inward agreement becomes fleeting hypocrisy and dissimulation.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم لا توافقهم في الظاهر كما لا توافقهمفي الباطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opponents, immersed in vice and shifting desires, flatter in turn and add this vice to their others, hoping the Prophet will reciprocate their compromise.
rows.anchor: أما هم فلانهماكهم في الرذائل وتعمقهم في التلون والاختلاف لتشعب أهوائهم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some distinguish blameworthy mudāhana, selling religion for worldly gain, from praiseworthy mudārā, giving up worldly interest for religion.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم المداهنة بيع الدين بالدنيا فهي من السيئات والمداراة بيع الدنيا بالدين

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic saying that he was commanded to show courteous accommodation to people, just as he was commanded to convey the message, does not license improper compromise.
rows.anchor: أمرت بمداراة الناس كما أمرت بالتبليغ

rows.speaker: الإمام الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazālī says the motive for overlooking a fault distinguishes the two: overlooking to protect religion or reform one's brother is mudārā; doing so for self-interest, desires, or status is mudāhana.
rows.anchor: في إحياء الفرق بين المداراة والمداهنة بالغرض الباعث على الإغضاء

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: Abū al-Dardāʾ says one may smile in the faces of people while the heart condemns them; Bursevī presents this as courteous accommodation toward someone whose harm is feared.
rows.anchor: وهذا معنى المداراة وهو مع من يخاف شره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ḥallāf is one who swears frequently in truth and falsehood, ignorant of the oath's sanctity and heedless of perjury because of bad belief.
rows.anchor: كثير الحلف في الحق والباطل لجهله حرمة اليمين وعدم مبالاته من الحنث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This trait is placed first among the qualities that forbid obedience because it is especially forceful as a warning.
rows.anchor: لكونه أدخل في الزجر قال في الكشاف

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf says frequent oath-taking alone is enough to admonish habitual swearers, and compares the warning with the prohibition against making God an excuse for oaths.
rows.anchor: وكفى به مزجرة لمن اعتاد الحلف ومثله قوله تعالى : [البقرة : 90]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ in the preceding challenge is read as transitive, or alternatively as indicating accompaniment, in the condition that they be truthful.
rows.anchor: فالباء للتعية ويجوز أن تكون للمصاحبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers have no rational proof for equating the righteous with the wicked, no revealed book, and no binding divinely confirmed pledges; no thoughtful people agree with them, so even imitation cannot support their claim.
rows.anchor: ليس لهم دليل عقلي في إثبات هذا المذهب وهو التسوية بين المحسن والمسيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage signals that a judge should investigate widely for truth in matters not immediately clear; judgment without inquiry is faulty even if accidentally correct, as shown by the rulings on prayer toward an unknown qibla.
rows.anchor: إلى أن اللائق بالحاكم تحري الصواب بقر اوسع فيما ليس بحاضر عنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm is governed by an omitted udhkur, and ʿan sāq stands in the passive as the deputy subject of yukshafu.
rows.anchor: يوم منصوب باذكر المقدر وعن ساق قائم مقام الفاعل ليكشف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means the Day of Resurrection, when distress becomes severe; it is an idiom, like saying a miser's hand is tied, with no literal hand-binding or uncovering of a shin.
rows.anchor: وكشف الساق مثل في ذلك ولا كشف ولا ساق ثمة كما تقول للأقطع الشحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The composite image likens the gathering's afflicted people to modest women forced to hike their skirts to flee a terrifying emergency; the simile is in the syntactic configuration, not the individual words.
rows.anchor: من غير تصرف في مفردات التركيب بل التصرف إنما هو في الهيئة التركيبية

rows.speaker: الفناري
rows.claim: Al-Fanārī says the uncovered shin represents an immense eschatological ordeal; Arabs say war has uncovered its shin when its severity is great, and the shins merging signal horrors piled together.
rows.anchor: قال المولى الفناري في تفسير الفاتحة فالساق التي كشفت لهم عبارة عن أمر عظيم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view takes sāq as the foundation that sustains a thing, like a tree or human leg, so unveiling it means the roots and realities of affairs become manifest.
rows.anchor: وقيل ساق الشيء أصله الذي به قوامه كساق الشجر وساق الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the severe-event interpretation, the indefinite form magnifies terror; on the foundational-reality interpretation, it conveys exaltation.
rows.anchor: وتنكيره على الوجه الأول للتهويل لأن يوم القيامة يوم يقع فيه أمر فظيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people summoned are unbelievers and hypocrites, called to prostrate as rebuke for having abandoned it in worldly life and to deepen their regret.
rows.anchor: توبيخا وتعنيفاف على تركهم إياه في الدنيا وتحسيرا لهم على تفريطهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call is not a renewed obligation to worship, since the Resurrection is not a time of legal duty or ritual worship.
rows.anchor: لأن يوم القيامة لا يكون فيه تعيد ولا تكليف وسيأتي غير هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their inability results from losing the real capacity, means, and bodily instruments needed to prostrate; the verse implies they do attempt it but cannot succeed.
rows.anchor: لزوال القدرة الحقيقية عليه وسلامة الأسباب والآلات وفيه دلالة على أنهم يقصدون السجود

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says their backs become a single vertebra, unable to bend when rising or bowing, so they remain standing and their regret grows; a hadith likewise says their backs remain one solid segment.
rows.anchor: ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه تعقم أصلابهم أي ترد عظاما بلا مفاصل لا تنثني

rows.speaker: أبو موسى
rows.claim: Abū Mūsā reports the Prophet's account: communities follow what they worshipped; the monotheists recognize God by His uniqueness, see Him when the veil is lifted, and prostrate, while others with rigid backs cannot; each believer is given a Jew or Christian in the Fire in his place.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بردة عن أبي موسى رضي الله عنه قال سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بقول إذا كان يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
rows.claim: When Abū Bardah relayed the report, ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz swore that it came from his father and said he had heard no report from the monotheists he liked more.
rows.anchor: والله الذي لا إله إلا هو أحدثك أبوك بهذا الحديث فحلفت له بثلاث إيمان فقال

rows.speaker: الفناري
rows.claim: Al-Fanārī describes the community remaining with its hypocrites, who reject an initial manifestation and recognize God only when He appears in the familiar form marked by their sign; true worshippers prostrate, while those who prostrated in ostentation are made to fall backward.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير الفاتحة للفناري رحمه الله يتجلى الحق في ذلك اليوم فيقول لتتبع كل أمة ما كانت عبد

rows.speaker: الفناري
rows.claim: Al-Fanārī says people on the Heights with equal scales are called to prostrate; this is the remaining duty in the Hereafter, and their prostration tips their good deeds so they enter Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقال أيضا يكون عى الأعراف من تساوت كفتا ميزانه فهم ينظرون إلى النار

rows.speaker: الأشاعرة
rows.claim: On the question of assigning a task that cannot be fulfilled, Ashʿarites permit it and Muʿtazilites forbid it; no one permits assigning what is intrinsically irrational, such as annihilating the eternal.
rows.anchor: وقد أجاز الأشاعرة التكليف به ومنعه المعتزلة وإما المحال العقلي وهو الممتنع لذاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khāshiʿatan is a circumstantial accusative connected with those summoned, and their eyes are its grammatical subject.
rows.anchor: حال من مروفع يدعون على أن أبصارهم مرتفع به على الفاعلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humility is attributed to the eyes because its effects show there, although all limbs are humbled and the heart is the true source of humility.
rows.anchor: ونسبة الخشوع إلى الأبصار لظهور أثره فيها وإلا فالأعضاء أيضا خاشعة ذليلة

rows.speaker: الكشافي
rows.claim: Al-Kāshifī glosses the description as people with lowered eyes, heads bowed and ashamed.
rows.anchor: يعني خداوندان أبصار سر دريش افكنده

rows.speaker: أبو الليث
rows.claim: Abū al-Layth says Muslims' faces become white as snow after prostration, while Jews, Christians, and hypocrites who could not prostrate grieve and have blackened faces.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الليث وذلك إن المسلمين إذا رفعوا رؤوسهم من السجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tarhaquhum means that disgrace reaches and envelops them; rahq denotes one thing covering another.
rows.anchor: تلحقهم وتغشاهم فإن الرهق غشيان الشيء الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhilla is severe humiliating disgrace, glossed by the root's forms for abasement and the adjective dhalīl, humiliated.
rows.anchor: شديدة تخزيهم كأنه تفسير لخشوع أبصارهم يقال ذل يذل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In worldly life they had been summoned by an obligatory call to prostrate; explicit wording replaces a pronoun for emphasis, or because prostration stands for prayer and its prostrations.
rows.anchor: لزيادة التقرير أولأن المراد به الصلاة أو ما فيها من السجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prostration is singled out because it is the greatest act of obedience.
rows.anchor: وخص السجود بالذكر من حيث إنه أعظم الطاعات

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the summons came through God's call, implicitly in the command to establish prayer or explicitly through the Prophet's call; one Prophetic report says a servant is closest to the Lord while prostrating and should supplicate much.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم يدعون بدعوة الله ريحا مثل قوله تعالى : [القلم : 43]{واسجدوا واعبدوا}

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet's instruction to pray the five prayers, fast the month, give zakat, and obey the commands promised entry into the Lord's Paradise is presented as an implicit invitation to prostrate.
rows.anchor: كقوله علي السلام صلوا خمسكم وصوموا شهركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars in every age also invite people to prostrate; the call of the adhān and iqāma, especially ḥayya ʿalā al-ṣalāh, is unmistakable, and answering willingly brings felicity.
rows.anchor: فإن قولهم حي على الصلاة دعوة بلا مرية فطوبى لمن أجاب دعوتهم بطوع لا بإكراه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause wa-hum sālimūn is circumstantial, describing those summoned in worldly life.
rows.anchor: حال من ضمير يدعون وهم سالمون} حال من مرفوع يدعون الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were healthy, with sound limbs and joints and fully able to prostrate and answer the call; they rejected it then and now have only regret.
rows.anchor: أي أصحاء في الدنيا سلمت أعضاؤهم ومفاصلهم من الآفات والعلل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qāriʿa is another name for the Hour because it strikes people with terrors: the sky splits, earth and mountains are crushed, and stars are extinguished.
rows.anchor: من جملة أسماء الساعة أيضا لأنها تقرع الناس أي تضرب بفنون الإفزاع والأهوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name replaces a pronoun for al-Ḥāqqa to foreground the striking terror and intensify the description of its severity.
rows.anchor: ووضعت موضع ضمير الحاقة للدلالة على معنى القرع فيها زيادة في وصف شدتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qawāriʿ al-Qurʾān can refer to verses recited in fear of jinn or people, such as Āyat al-Kursī, which strike hearts with God's majesty and seek His protection and mercy.
rows.anchor: للآيات التي تقرأ حين افزع من الجن والإنس لقرع قلوب المؤذين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning about the Hour and its terrors threatens Meccans with the outcome of denying resurrection and gathering.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية تخويف لأهل مكة من عاقبة تكذيبهم بالبعث والحشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamūd were Arabs whose homes lay at al-Ḥijr between Syria and the Ḥijāz, a place Syrian pilgrims pass on their journeys.
rows.anchor: وكانوا عربا منازلهم بالحجر بين الشأن والحجاز يراها حجاج الشأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive reports that they were destroyed, since the actor, God, is already known and the event is what matters.
rows.anchor: أي أهلكهم الله لتكذيبهم فأخبر عن الفعل لأنه المراد دون الفاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭāghiya is an extraordinarily violent blast, exceeding other cries in force and making earth and hearts quake.
rows.anchor: أي بالصيحة التي جاوزت عن حد سائر الصيحات في الشدة فرجفب منها الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The quake and the blast refer to the same Thamūd event, reconciling the account that says the quake seized them with the account that says the cry did.
rows.anchor: فأخذتهم الرجفة} وبين قوله تعالى : فأخذتهم الصيحة والقصة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamūd symbolize people of outward learning veiled from true inward knowledge; because they rejected the inward path and failed to follow a genuine saint, God destroyed them with the fire of distance and veiling, leaving spiritual corruption beneath outward rectitude.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى أهل العلم الظاهر المحجوبين عن العلوم الحقيقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀd lived in al-Aḥqāf, the sands from Oman toward Ḥaḍramawt and Yemen; they were Arabs of imposing stature, with the tallest a hundred cubits, the shortest sixty, and heads like domes.
rows.anchor: وكانت منازلهم بالأحقاف وهي الرمل بين عمان إلى حضر موت واليمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀd follows Thamūd because of the chronological order, which also progresses from the less to the more deeply misguided.
rows.anchor: وتأخيره عن ثمود من تقدمهم زمانا من قبيل الترقي من الضال الشديد

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The wind is identified as the west wind on the basis of the Prophetic saying that the east wind brought victory while the west wind destroyed ʿĀd.
rows.anchor: نصرت بالصبا وأهلكت عاد بالدبور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣarṣar describes a wind with a harsh, loud whistling or squealing sound as it blows.
rows.anchor: أي شديدة الصوت لها صرصرة في هبوبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian verse pictures wrathful blasts turning people to dust until even their dust leaves no trace.
rows.anchor: وعاصفات قضا ازمهب قهر وزيد شدند خاك وازان خاك نيزنيست نشان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wise should strive for a second life through enduring truthful remembrance; Abraham's prayer for a good name among later generations points to this, while true lasting life comes through divine unveiling and universal effusion.
rows.anchor: حتى يبقى في الدنيا بالعمر الثاني كما دل عليه قوله تعالى حكاية عن إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Pharaoh intended is the Pharaoh of Moses, singled out because of his extreme arrogance and self-exaltation.
rows.anchor: أي فرعون موسى أفرده بالذكر لغاية علوه واستكباره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the primary reading, man qablahu means the unbelievers who preceded Pharaoh, other than ʿĀd and Thamūd; this is a general statement after specific mention.
rows.anchor: ومن صولة وقبل نقيض بعد

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو ويعقوب والكسائي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr, Yaʿqūb, and al-Kisāʾī read qibalihi with kasra on qāf and fatḥa on bāʾ, meaning Pharaoh's contemporaries among the Copts and Egyptians.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو ويعقوب والكسائي قبله بكسر القاف وفتح الباء بمعنى ومن معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Muʾtafikāt refers to the towns of Lot, called overturned because God overturned them upon their people by sinking them.
rows.anchor: أي قرى قوم لوط أي ألها لأنها عطفت على ما قبلها من فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The towns are counted as five, named here Ṣaʿbah, Ṣaʿdah, ʿUmrah, Dūmā, and Sodom; Lot's people are singled out after the general grouping because their indecency was unprecedented.
rows.anchor: وهي خمس قريات صعبه وصعده وعمره ودوما سدم وهي أعظم القرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ may indicate accompaniment or, more apparently, causation; al-khāṭiʾa can be a verbal noun meaning error or heedlessness, or an adjective for grave sinful deeds.
rows.anchor: الباء للملابسة والتعدية وهو الأظهر أي بالخطأ أو بالغفلة أو الأفعال ذات الخطأ العظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the verbal-noun reading al-khāṭiʾa is like ʿāqiba; on the other readings it modifies an omitted noun, and the preferred analysis is metaphorical attribution, as in shāʿir poetry.
rows.anchor: فالخاطئة على الأول مصدر كالعاقبة وعلى الأخيرين صفة لمحذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each community disobeyed its own messenger; rasūl functions collectively because this noun form can be invariant for gender and number, and the generic possessive is distributive across the communities.
rows.anchor: فعصى كل أمة رسولهم حين نهاهم عما كانوا يتعاطونه من القبائح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God seized each of those communities with punishment.
rows.anchor: أي الله تعالى بالعقوبة أي كل قوم منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their seizure exceeded the severity customary among people or the punishment of other unbelievers because their sins were more heinous; rābiya derives from the sense of increase.
rows.anchor: أي زائدة في الشدة على عقوبات سائر الكفار أو على القدر المعروف عند الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Examples include drowning Noah's rejecters, overturning and stoning Lot's towns before burying them in foul water, and drowning Pharaoh's troops in the Red Sea or Nile; each people received fitting recompense.
rows.anchor: أغرق من كذب نوحا وهم كل أهل الأرض غير من ركب معه في السفينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These punishments warn Quraysh against denial and provide an awakening lesson for people of understanding.
rows.anchor: وفي كل ذلك تخويف لقريش وتحذير لهم عن التكذيب وفيه عبرة موقظة لأولي الألباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root rabā means to grow or increase; legal ribā is the extra amount the creditor takes beyond what was lent.
rows.anchor: ربا الشيء يربو إذ زاد ومنه الربا الشرعي وهو الفضل الذي يأخذه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water is the familiar floodwater of Noah's time, which exceeded its normal bounds; one report says it rose five hundred cubits above everything.
rows.anchor: تى ارتفع على كل شيء خمسمائة ذراع

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another report says the flood rose fifteen cubits above the highest mountain; an alternative account describes a level the angels assigned to control it could not contain.
rows.anchor: أو حده في المعاملة مع خزنة من الملائكة بحيث لم يقدروا على ضبطه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The flood's excess was caused by Noah's people persisting in disbelief, sins, and denial of his revealed teachings, including matters of the Resurrection; God avenged them by drowning.
rows.anchor: بسبب إصرار قوم نوح على فنون الكفر والمعاصي ومبالغتهم في تكذيبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people addressed are carried through their ancestors while still in their loins, so they are spoken of as personally carried; this highlights the favor, since their ancestors' rescue enabled their descendants to exist.
rows.anchor: أيها الناس أي حملنا آباءكم وأنتم في أصلابكم فكأنكم محمولون بأشخاصكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Jāriya is Noah's ship, so named because it runs upon water; being carried in it means being lifted above the flood until it subsided.
rows.anchor: يعني في سفينة نوح لأن من شأنها أن تجري على الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition fī is not governed directly by ḥamalnā; it belongs to an omitted circumstantial phrase describing the carried people as protected aboard the moving ship.
rows.anchor: فإنها ليست بصلة للحمل بل متعلقة بمحذوف هو حال من مفعوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their rescue depended solely on God's protection; the ship was only an apparent, formal cause, not the true source of safety.
rows.anchor: مدار نجاتهم محض عصمته تعالى وإنما السفينة سبب صوري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rescue and drowning serve as a reminder of the Creator's power, wisdom, overpowering force, and abundant mercy.
rows.anchor: عبرة ودلالة على كمال قدرة الصانع وحكمته وقوة قهره وسعة رحمته

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kāshifī says the ship is made a reminder and lesson through the believers' rescue and the unbelievers' destruction; Kashf al-Asrār says it remains a memorial as long as the world exists.
rows.anchor: وقال الكاشفي) : نا كردانيم آن كشتى رابراي شماندى وعبرتي درنجات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earliest generations of this community are said to have encountered the Ark, whose planks were on Mount al-Jūdī.
rows.anchor: وقد أدرك السفينة أوائل هذه الأمة وكان ألوحها على الجودي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʿīhā means to preserve it; waʿy is retaining something within oneself, as in remembering what was said.
rows.anchor: أي تحفظا وبالفارسية ونكاه دارداين ندرا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic saying describes the good life as belonging to a learned speaker and a listener who comprehends.
rows.anchor: لا خير في العيش إلا العالم ناطق ومستمع واع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Īʿāʾ is preserving something outside oneself in a container, as when goods are placed in a vessel.
rows.anchor: والإيعاء أن تحفظه في غير نفسك من وعاء يقال أوعيت المتاع في الوعاء

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet told Asmāʾ, daughter of Abū Bakr, not to hoard or withhold, lest God withhold from her, and to give what she could.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام : لا سماء بنت أبي بكر رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The segment quotes an anonymous poet: good endures however long, while evil is the foulest provision one can store up.
rows.anchor: الخير يبقى وإن طال الزمان به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An aware ear retains what should be remembered and pondered, and does not squander it by failing to act upon it.
rows.anchor: أي أذن من شأنها أن تحفظ ما يجب حفظه بتذكره والتفكر فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Awareness belongs to the heart, but ears convey reports to receptive hearts, so the ear is described with the heart's quality.
rows.anchor: يقال الوعي فعل القلب ولكن الآذان تؤدي الحديث إلى القلوب الواعية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular indefinite ear, instead of plural definite ears, signals scarcity; even one such ear can lead to the rescue and continued life of multitudes.
rows.anchor: والتنكير والتوحيد حيث لم يقل الآذان الواعية للدلالة على قلتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One who preserves the story can remind people, encourage saving faith, and warn them away from destructive disbelief, thereby helping ensure communal survival and continuity.
rows.anchor: إن من وعي هذه القصة إنما يعيها ويحفظها لأجل أن يذكرها للناس

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf says that one ear which understands God counts as the great majority in God's sight, even if everyone else fills the space between the horizons.
rows.anchor: قال في الكشاف الأذن الواحدة إذا وعت وعقلت عن الله فهي السواد الأعظم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic saying calls successful the person whom God grants an aware heart; Bursevī also reports the Prophet asking that this verse become ʿAlī's ear, after which ʿAlī says he forgot nothing.
rows.anchor: عن النبي عليه السلام إنه قال لعلي رضي الله عنه نزول هذه الآية سألت الله أن يجعلها إذنك

rows.speaker: النقاش
rows.claim: Al-Naqqāsh gives another version in which the Prophet takes ʿAlī by the ear and says, This is the ear meant.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية أخذ بأذن علي بن أبي طالب وقال هي هذه ذكره النقاش

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the aware ears were named by God in eternity and hear every address from Him.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : تلك آذان اسمها الله في الأزل خطابه

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra explains his many reports by saying the emigrants and helpers were occupied with earning, while he stayed with the Prophet and was content with little; after the Prophet promised that whoever spread his cloak would retain the sermon, Abū Hurayra did so and never forgot the words.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي هريرة إنه قيل على إنك تكثر رواية الحايث وغيرك لا بروى مثلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account illustrates the effect of eloquent speech; otherwise the Prophet's prayer alone would have sufficed for retention, as in ʿAlī's case.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى تأثير حسن المقال وفائدته وإلا لكان دعاؤه عليه السلام كافيا
